context.guidance: Set up alerting or scheduled review on the access logs and authentication events for every store that holds Personal Data, so unauthorised access is detected and its cause and impact can be established. Rule 6(1)(c) requires monitoring and review of this kind, and investigation depends on it. Make sure the alert rules cover authentication failures and privileged reads, not only application errors.

value.fix: Enable and centralise access and authentication logging for every store that holds Personal Data, then add alert rules and a scheduled review. Alerts should cover authentication failures (repeated failed logins, lockouts, logins from unusual sources), privileged or bulk reads of Personal Data, and changes to access permissions, not only application errors. Route the logs to a central store with retention long enough to investigate incidents, assign an owner for alert triage, and document periodic log reviews with sign-off to satisfy Rule 6(1)(c). Test the alert rules with simulated failed logins and privileged reads to confirm they fire. The supplied evidence is a page title, 'Solved $difficulties Star Challenges', which contains an unrendered template placeholder ($difficulties). It does not show a monitoring gap, so first identify which stores in this project hold Personal Data and confirm their current logging, then fix the placeholder as a separate bug.
